title: Resonance and a failed uniqueness claim
promptMarkdown: Assume $f\in L^2(0,1)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. Solve the compatibility question for $-u''-\alpha u=f$, u(0)=u(1)=0. State when there is a unique L² spectral solution, what condition is necessary and sufficient when α=(kπ)², and the family of solutions in that case. For f=e_k decide solvability at resonance. Here a spectral solution is required to belong to the Dirichlet operator domain: in the sine basis its coefficients satisfy $\sum_n(n\pi)^4|u_n|^2<\infty$. If $f$ is continuous, also explain why the solution is classical ($C^2$ with zero endpoint values).
hintLadder: Expand both sides in the sine basis.
At a vanishing denominator separate compatibility from nonuniqueness.
